title: October 27, 1904: a revolutionary was born who would die 63 days into a hunger strike, demanding dignity for political prisoners.

sources.text: Sabrang India - Remembering the independence activist, Jatindra Nath Das

caption:
October 27, 1904: a revolutionary was born who would die 63 days into a hunger strike, demanding dignity for political prisoners.

Arrested in the Lahore Conspiracy Case alongside Bhagat Singh, he launched a hunger strike in Lahore Jail on July 13, 1929, demanding Indian political prisoners get the same treatment as European prisoners - better food, reading material and no humiliating searches.

His death triggered mass protests and funeral processions across India and is credited with influencing how political detainees were treated in prisons for years afterward.

Das never lived to see independence - but the standard he died demanding became part of how a free India would later treat anyone in its custody.
